    13	\author{}
    14	\date{2026-09-03}
    15	
    16	\begin{document}
    17	\maketitle
    18	
    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The extraction proof contains two
    23	  incorrect numerical steps and later suppresses the range projection when
    24	  passing from unitary conjugation to isometry conjugation.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} A corrected positive-contraction estimate,
    26	  a small-error case split for normalization, and one range-projection transfer
    27	  lemma for a projective measurement family.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Positivity, contraction inequalities,
    29	  isometry range projections, and norm estimates belong to finite-dimensional
    30	  Hilbert-space algebra.  The state-dependent family distance and register
    31	  placements are project-local.
    32	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The inequality
    33	  $H^2\geq2H-I$ for a positive contraction, the triangle inequality, and
    34	  $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$ for an isometry.  The repair is tracked in
    35	  \ghissue{19}.
    36	\end{itemize}
    37	
    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.
    69	
    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.
   118	
   119	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   120	
   121	The proof of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} and the soundness proof in
   122	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} use the corrected
   123	positive-contraction estimate, make the small-error case distinction explicit,
   124	and isolate the range-projection calculation.  The chapter therefore preserves
   125	the source's state and observable conclusions while exposing the omitted
   126	argument.
   127	
   128	The structure \path{ExtractionWitness} in
   129	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Unitary.lean} contains only the two-sided
   130	unitarity equations for the concrete swap maps, a normalized auxiliary state,
   131	the transformed-state estimate, and the two-player Pauli-projector comparison.
   132	The theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness} concludes the existence of this
   133	data at the explicit extraction scale from the projective strategy and its
   134	\path{GlobalPairWitness}; it assumes no range-projection transfer, bridge, or
   135	residual package.  Thus these declarations match the Stage~4.2 extraction
   136	lemma, including the corrected numerical estimates, but do not formalize the
   137	later passage to the isometries in the soundness theorem.  No declaration yet
   138	states that passage.
   139	
   140	Issue~\#19 owns this concrete Stage~4.2 interface and discrepancy record.
   141	\ghissue{47} owns the Stage~4.3 proof of
   142	\path{exists_extractionWitness} and the separate range-projection theorem
   143	needed by \path{pauli_soundness}; that theorem must be derived from the
   144	concrete data rather than stored in the witness.
   145	
   146	\section{Conclusion}
   147	
   148	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   149	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   150	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   151	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   152	the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
   153	already supplied by the extraction lemma.

    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    41	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    42	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    43	correlation estimate
    44	\[
    45	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    46	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    47	\]
    48	It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
    49	binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
    50	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    51	\[
    52	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    53	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    54	\]
    55	Moreover,
    56	\[
    57	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    58	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    59	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
    60	\]
    61	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    62	observable is invertible.
    63	
    64	The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    65	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
    66	the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
    67	is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
    68	formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space
    69	uniform over $(x,z)$.
    70	
    71	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
    72	
    73	Lines~711--725 of
    74	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
    75	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
    76	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
    77	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
    78	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The quotation
    79	also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem and would
    80	unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect.  The assertion
    81	at the identity follows from exact linearity as above.
    82	
    83	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
    84	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
    85	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
    86	many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
    87	to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
    88	
    89	The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
    90	with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
    91	returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
    92	one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
    93	orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
    94	observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
    95	chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
    96	or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.
    97	
    98	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    99	
   100	Theorem~\path{thm:linearity} and
   101	Remark~\path{rem:linearity-import} in
   102	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex} record respectively the
   103	averaged provider theorem and the common-ancilla obligation for its fiberwise
   104	use.  The relevant material is at lines~98--147 and 149--191 of that chapter.
   105	
   106	The declaration \path{exists_exactly_linear_observables} in
   107	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean} assumes a nonnegative defect, a
   108	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, binary observables, and the averaged
   109	three-observable correlation.  It returns one finite ancillary space and
   110	normalized ancillary vector for that family, exactly linear binary observables
   111	on the extension, and only the averaged squared-distance bound with the same
   112	defect.  It neither assumes $\delta\leq1$ nor asserts pointwise closeness.  Its
   113	statement therefore matches the provider-faithful blueprint theorem rather
   114	than the strengthened quotation in the QPBT paper.  Its proof remains open,
   115	and no Lean declaration yet supplies the finite common-extension construction
   116	for the family indexed by $(x,z)$.
   117	
   118	Issue~\#19 introduced this discrepancy record for the extraction skeleton;
   119	\ghissue{47} owns the Stage~4.3 proof work consumed downstream.  The chapter-16
   120	extraction declarations consume the concrete \path{GlobalPairWitness}; they
   121	do not assume a new fiberwise linearity hypothesis or a common ancillary space.
   122	
   123	\section{Conclusion}
   124	
   125	The primary discrepancy is a quantifier mismatch in the quotation: the cited
   126	linearity theorem gives average, not pointwise, closeness.  Its use for the
   127	family indexed by $(x,z)$ also requires an explicit finite common-extension
   128	argument.  Both are open formal reductions compatible with the intended
   129	source conclusion.

     3	/-!
     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52	
    53	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
    54	`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    61	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    62	
    63	/--
    64	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    65	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    67	-/
    68	noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    69	    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
    70	  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)
    71	
    72	/--
    73	The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
    74	Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `def:indicator-vector` in the
    75	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    77	-/
    78	theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    79	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :
    80	    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by
    81	  simp [lowDegreeEnc, lowDegreeEncoding, indicatorVec, dotProduct]
    82	
    83	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-! # Decoding maps for the low-degree code
     4	
     5	This file supplies `def:decoding-map` and the Boolean cube embedding from
     6	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
     7	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`.  The specialization to
     8	polynomial representatives is `decodeFqRep`; its restriction to the bounded
     9	class `Poly` is defined in `Algebra/Decoding`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    17	
    18	/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by
    19	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    20	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    21	def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
    22	  | false => 0
    23	  | true => 1
    24	
    25	/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
    26	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    27	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    28	def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
    29	  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)
    30	
    31	/-- On the Boolean cube, an indicator polynomial evaluates to the corresponding
    32	Kronecker delta.  This is the interpolation observation at paper lines 880-891. -/
    33	private theorem eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    34	    (y z : Cube m) :
    35	    MvPolynomial.eval (cubeEmbed (K := K) z) (indicatorPoly (K := K) y) =
    36	      if y = z then 1 else 0 := by
    37	  classical
    38	  rw [indicatorPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_prod]
    39	  simp only [apply_ite, MvPolynomial.eval_X, MvPolynomial.eval_sub, map_one]
    40	  have hfactor (i : Fin m) :
    41	      (if y i then cubeEmbed (K := K) z i else 1 - cubeEmbed (K := K) z i) =
    42	        if y i = z i then 1 else 0 := by
    43	    cases hy : y i <;> cases hz : z i <;> simp_all [cubeEmbed, boolToScalar]
    44	  simp_rw [hfactor]
    45	  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
    46	  split_ifs <;> simp_all [funext_iff]
    47	
    48	/-- Evaluating a low-degree encoding at an embedded Boolean point recovers its
    49	coefficient at that point, as stated at paper line 891. -/
    50	private theorem lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    51	    (a : Cube m → K) (z : Cube m) :
    52	    lowDegreeEnc a (cubeEmbed z) = a z := by
    53	  rw [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
    54	  simp [dotProduct, indicatorVec, eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed]
    55	
    56	/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    57	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    58	noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    59	    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    60	  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    63	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    64	noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    65	    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    66	  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g
    67	
    68	/-- The full-field specialization of `decodeAt` for arbitrary polynomial
    69	representatives.  Its restriction to bounded representatives is defined in
    70	`Algebra/Decoding.lean`.
    71	Every value is retained because the filter is `H = Finset.univ`, so this is the
    72	cube-indexed evaluation of a polynomial representative.  The restricted
    73	decoder identity remains separate and is only available for encoding
    74	representatives; no unrestricted interpolation identity is asserted here.
    75	
    76	This is the `H = \F_q` reading of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, used by Chapter 16 at
    78	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20`; paper origin
    79	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420` and
    80	the correction recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
    81	noncomputable def decodeFqRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    82	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Cube m → K :=
    83	  decodeAt (Finset.univ : Finset K) (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x g)
    84	
    85	/-- A polynomial representative lies in the low-degree encoding image when it
    86	is exactly the multilinear representative reconstructed from its full-field
    87	decoder.  This predicate is used to state the support restriction required by
    88	the Chapter 16 decoding argument; it does not identify arbitrary polynomial
    89	functions with their representatives.
    90	
    91	See `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-116`. -/
    92	def IsEncodingRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    93	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Prop :=
    94	  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFqRep g) = g
    95	
    96	/-- The restricted decoding identity in `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    97	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    98	theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    99	    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
   100	    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
   101	  funext y
   102	  simp [decodeAt, lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed, ha y]
   103	
   104	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    79	/-- A strategy-local register paired with one generalized-Pauli register. This
    80	is the operator space in `def:expanded-observables`, paper
    81	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`. -/
    82	abbrev ExpandedLocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :=
    83	  S.LocalSpace side × PauliRegister P
    84	
    85	/-- The strategy state tensored with EPR states on `A'A''` and `B'B''`, in the
    86	six-register order. This is `eq:def-psihat`, paper
    87	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    88	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    89	noncomputable def psiHat (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    90	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    91	  classical
    92	  exact
    93	    reindexState (sixRegShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    94	      (vecTensor
    95	        (vecTensor S.toStrategy.ψ (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    96	        (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    97	
    98	/-- Place an operator on one of `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, or `AB''`, with the
    99	identity on all remaining registers. The input local space is determined by
   100	the placement, so no equality between the player spaces is assumed. Paper
   101	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
   102	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
   103	noncomputable def place (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   104	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   105	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   106	  fun i j =>
   107	    match p with
   108	    | .AA' =>
   109	        O (i.1.1, i.1.2.1) (j.1.1, j.1.2.1) *
   110	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   111	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   112	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   113	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   114	    | .BA'' =>
   115	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   116	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   117	          O (i.2.1, i.1.2.2) (j.2.1, j.1.2.2) *
   118	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   119	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   120	    | .BB' =>
   121	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   122	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   123	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   124	          O (i.2.1, i.2.2.1) (j.2.1, j.2.2.1) *
   125	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   126	    | .AB'' =>
   127	        O (i.1.1, i.2.2.2) (j.1.1, j.2.2.2) *
   128	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   129	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   130	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   131	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1
   132	
   133	/-- The expanded observable
   134	`W^r(u) tensor tau^W(r * ind_m(u))` on a selected player side. This is
   135	Equation `eq:lc-23`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`,
   136	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:783-807`. -/
   137	noncomputable def expObs (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (r : PauliScalar P) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   139	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   140	  heteroKron (S.pointObs side W r u)
   141	    (tauObservable W (fun h => r * indicatorVec u h))
   142	
   143	/-- The Fourier average defining the expanded point effect. This is the first
   144	display of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   145	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   146	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   147	noncomputable def expPointOp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   148	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   149	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   150	  averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) fun r =>
   151	    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)) • S.expObs side W r u
   152	
   153	/-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding has
   154	value `a` at `u`. This is Equation `eq:qld-point-obs-def`, paper
   155	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:389-394`, blueprint
   156	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   157	noncomputable def tauPointProj (W : PauliKind)
   158	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=
   159	  ∑ h ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun h : PauliRegister P =>
   160	      dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = a),
   161	    pauliProj W h
   162	
   163	/-- Expanded point effects are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity
   164	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   165	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   166	theorem expPointOp_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   167	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   168	    0 ≤ S.expPointOp side W u a := by
   169	  sorry
   170	
   171	/-- Expanded point effects sum to the identity. This is the completeness
   172	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   173	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   174	theorem expPointOp_sum_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   175	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   176	    ∑ a, S.expPointOp side W u a = 1 := by
   177	  sorry
   178	
   179	/-- The complete expanded point measurement on the chosen player and Pauli
   180	register. Its effects are those of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   181	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   182	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   183	noncomputable def pointMeasExp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   184	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   185	    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   186	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (S.expPointOp side W u)
   187	    (S.expPointOp_nonneg side W u) (S.expPointOp_sum_eq_one side W u)
   188	
   189	/-- The expanded point effect is the convolution of the strategy point
   190	measurement and the Pauli-register point projection. This is the final display
   191	of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   192	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   193	theorem expPointOp_eq_convolution (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   194	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   195	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
   196	    S.expPointOp side W u a =
   197	      ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
   198	          p.1 + p.2 = a),
   199	        heteroKron ((S.pointMeas side W u).effect p.1)
   200	          (tauPointProj W u p.2) := by
   201	  sorry
   202	
   203	/-- The expanded point measurement is projective, as asserted after the
   204	convolution formula in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   205	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   206	theorem pointMeasExp_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   207	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   208	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.pointMeasExp side W u) := by
   209	  sorry
   210	
   211	/-- Trace-coarse-graining of the expanded point measurement. This is Equation
   212	`eq:qld-def-mptur`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`,
   213	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   214	noncomputable def expPointTrace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   215	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   216	    (r : PauliScalar P) : Measurement (ZMod 2) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   217	  (S.pointMeasExp side W u).postprocess fun a => fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)
   218	
   219	/-- Fourier inversion writes a trace-coarse-grained point effect as one half
   220	of the identity plus its signed expanded observable. This is Equation
   221	`eq:lc-22`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`, blueprint
   222	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   223	theorem expPointTrace_eq_half_add (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   224	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   225	    (r : PauliScalar P) (b : ZMod 2) :
   226	    (S.expPointTrace side W u r).effect b =
   227	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   228	        (1 + phaseSign b • S.expObs side W r u) := by
   229	  sorry
   230	
   231	end ProjectiveSetting
   232	
   233	end
   234	
   235	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52	
    53	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
    54	`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    61	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    62	
    63	/--
    64	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    65	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    67	-/
    68	noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    69	    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
    70	  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)
    71	
    72	/--
    73	The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
    74	Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `def:indicator-vector` in the
    75	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    77	-/
    78	theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    79	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :
    80	    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by
    81	  simp [lowDegreeEnc, lowDegreeEncoding, indicatorVec, dotProduct]
    82	
    83	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Polynomial combination and restricted line distributions
     6	
     7	This file contains the concrete definitions at the foundation of the
     8	Chapter 15 combining argument.  A pair of bounded individual-degree
     9	polynomials is embedded into the two coordinate blocks of an extended
    10	polynomial.  On lines, explicit affine reparameterizations are composed with
    11	coefficient-list polynomials.  The original-dimensional restricted line laws
    12	are formed before decoding, while their field seed is still present.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The combining map is `def:combine-map` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`, with paper origin
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`.
    19	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line` in blueprint lines 578--592,
    20	with paper origin in the same source at lines 1038--1048.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-- The bounded individual-degree polynomial outcome used by the global
    33	pair measurement.  This is the actual `polyFunc` subtype from
    34	`def:polyfunc`, not a coefficient-box replacement. -/
    35	noncomputable abbrev Poly (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    36	  ↥(MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (PauliScalar P) P.d)
    37	
    38	/-- Pairs of bounded polynomial representatives returned by the global
    39	measurement in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    40	noncomputable abbrev PolyPair (P : AdmissibleParams) := Poly P × Poly P
    41	
    42	/-- Split the extended coordinate set into the `X` block, the `Z` block, and
    43	the two scalar coordinates.  This is formalization-only coordinate plumbing
    44	for `def:combine-map`, blueprint
    45	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`, paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    47	def finCombineEquiv (m : ℕ) :
    48	    Fin (2 * m + 2) ≃ ((Fin m ⊕ Fin m) ⊕ Fin 2) :=
    49	  (finCongr (by omega)).trans
    50	    (finSumFinEquiv.symm.trans
    51	      (Equiv.sumCongr finSumFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl (Fin 2))))
    52	
    53	/-- Embed an `X`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
    54	def embX (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    55	  fun i => (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inl i))

    39	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:475-505`, blueprint
    40	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:932-1032`. -/
    41	noncomputable def deltaAnticom (ε : ℝ) : ℝ :=

    44	/-- The concrete square-root error is polynomially small in the sense used by

    18	/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by

    27	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    28	def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
    29	  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)
    30	
    31	/-- On the Boolean cube, an indicator polynomial evaluates to the corresponding
    32	Kronecker delta.  This is the interpolation observation at paper lines 880-891. -/
    33	private theorem eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    34	    (y z : Cube m) :
    35	    MvPolynomial.eval (cubeEmbed (K := K) z) (indicatorPoly (K := K) y) =
    36	      if y = z then 1 else 0 := by
    37	  classical
    38	  rw [indicatorPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_prod]
    39	  simp only [apply_ite, MvPolynomial.eval_X, MvPolynomial.eval_sub, map_one]
    40	  have hfactor (i : Fin m) :
    41	      (if y i then cubeEmbed (K := K) z i else 1 - cubeEmbed (K := K) z i) =
    42	        if y i = z i then 1 else 0 := by
    43	    cases hy : y i <;> cases hz : z i <;> simp_all [cubeEmbed, boolToScalar]
    44	  simp_rw [hfactor]
    45	  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
    46	  split_ifs <;> simp_all [funext_iff]
    47	
    48	/-- Evaluating a low-degree encoding at an embedded Boolean point recovers its
    49	coefficient at that point, as stated at paper line 891. -/
    50	private theorem lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    51	    (a : Cube m → K) (z : Cube m) :
    52	    lowDegreeEnc a (cubeEmbed z) = a z := by
    53	  rw [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
    54	  simp [dotProduct, indicatorVec, eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed]
    55	
    56	/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    57	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    58	noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    59	    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    60	  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    63	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    64	noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    65	    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    66	  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g
    67	
    68	/-- The full-field specialization of `decodeAt` for arbitrary polynomial
    69	representatives.  Its restriction to bounded representatives is defined in
    70	`Algebra/Decoding.lean`.
    71	Every value is retained because the filter is `H = Finset.univ`, so this is the
    72	cube-indexed evaluation of a polynomial representative.  The restricted
    73	decoder identity remains separate and is only available for encoding
    74	representatives; no unrestricted interpolation identity is asserted here.
    75	
    76	This is the `H = \F_q` reading of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, used by Chapter 16 at
    78	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20`; paper origin
    79	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420` and
    80	the correction recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
    81	noncomputable def decodeFqRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    82	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Cube m → K :=
    83	  decodeAt (Finset.univ : Finset K) (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x g)
    84	
    85	/-- A polynomial representative lies in the low-degree encoding image when it
    86	is exactly the multilinear representative reconstructed from its full-field
    87	decoder.  This predicate is used to state the support restriction required by
    88	the Chapter 16 decoding argument; it does not identify arbitrary polynomial
    89	functions with their representatives.
    90	
    91	See `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-116`. -/
    92	def IsEncodingRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    93	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Prop :=
    94	  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFqRep g) = g
    95	
    96	/-- The restricted decoding identity in `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    97	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    98	theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    99	    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
   100	    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
   101	  funext y
   102	  simp [decodeAt, lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed, ha y]
   103	
   104	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5

     8	specialization to polynomial representatives live in
     9	`Algebra/LowDegreeCodeTheorems`; this module states the corresponding maps on
    10	`Poly P` used in the extraction chapter.

    13	
    14	The decoder is `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, with the extraction use
    16	at `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20` and paper
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1450`.
    18	The restricted decoder identity and its encoding hypothesis are documented in
    19	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`.

    31	
    32	This is polynomial evaluation on the source's `\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)` carrier.  It
    33	does not identify representatives that induce the same polynomial function. -/

    35	    (x : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliScalar P :=
    36	  MvPolynomial.eval x g.1

    42	`PauliScalar P` by `cubeEmbed`. -/
    43	noncomputable def decodeOn {P : AdmissibleParams}
    44	    (H : Finset (PauliScalar P)) (g : Poly P) : PauliRegister P :=
    45	  decodeAt H (fun x => evalPoly g x)

    47	/-- Full-field specialization of `decodeOn` used in Chapter 16.
    48	
    49	The retained-value set is `Finset.univ`, so every field value is kept.  This
    50	choice is the correction recorded in
    51	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
    52	noncomputable abbrev decodeOnUniv {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P) :
    53	    PauliRegister P :=

    35	/-- Select the polynomial belonging to a Pauli basis from a joint polynomial

    38	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:65-76`. -/
    39	def selectPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind) : PolyPair P -> Poly P

    48	/-- The single-basis marginal of the global polynomial-pair measurement.
    49	This is `def:s-w-marginals`, blueprint
    50	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:65-76`, paper
    51	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1421-1423`. -/
    52	noncomputable def marginalPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}

     3	/-!
     4	# Extraction foundations
     5	
     6	This module defines the register identifications used to pull the Pauli
     7	measurements apart. It retains the distinct local spaces of a
     8	heterogeneous strategy, coarse-grains the generalized Pauli projectors by a
     9	dot product, and records the state and error expressions needed by the later
    10	extraction witness.

    13	the basis stored in `P.model` and is not re-quantified here.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The Pauli dot-product projectors formalize `def:tau-dot-product-projector` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:85-93`, from
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.
    20	The register and state helpers support `def:tilde-m-measurement`,
    21	`def:v-swap-unitary`, and `lem:qld-unitary`, from paper lines 1429-1435 and
    22	1666-1713 and blueprint lines 104-113 and 301-375.

    33	/-! ## Heterogeneous extraction registers -/
    34	
    35	/-- One player's registers after adjoining the two generalized-Pauli
    36	registers: `AA'A''` or `BB'B''`. This identifies the register order and spaces for
    37	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713` and
    38	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:104-113,301-334`. -/
    39	abbrev ExtractionBlock (P : AdmissibleParams) (ι : Type*) :=
    40	  (ι × PauliRegister P) × PauliRegister P
    41	
    42	/-- The two heterogeneous extraction blocks in the order
    43	`AA'A'' | BB'B''`. This is the block presentation of the existing `SixReg`
    44	space used in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
    45	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
    46	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/

    48	  ExtractionBlock P ιA × ExtractionBlock P ιB

   180	    (N : α → Op ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) : Op ι :=

   188	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
   189	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Measurement α ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   190	    (M.postprocess f).effect b = bracketOp M.effect f b :=
   191	  rfl
   192	
   193	/-- The projector obtained by measuring in basis `W` and retaining outcomes
   194	whose dot product with `u` is `a`. This is Equation `eq:def-tauwu` in
   195	`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
   196	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:85-93`, paper
   197	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`. -/
   198	noncomputable def tauDotProj {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
   199	    (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=
   200	  bracketOp (pauliProj W) (fun h => dotProduct h u) a
   201	
   202	/-- Each dot-product coarse-graining is a projector, as asserted in
   203	`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
   204	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:85-93`, paper
   205	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.

   208	calculation. -/
   209	theorem tauDotProj_isProj {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
   210	    (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   211	    IsProj (tauDotProj W u a) := by
   212	  sorry
   213

   215	This is the completeness assertion of `def:tau-dot-product-projector`,
   216	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:85-93`, paper
   217	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.
   218	
   219	**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks completeness of the generalized-Pauli
   220	projector family. -/
   221	theorem sum_tauDotProj_eq_one {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
   222	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   223	    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, tauDotProj W u a = 1 := by
   224	  sorry

   226	/-! ## Conjugation and extraction error -/
   227	
   228	/-- Conjugation of an operator by a square matrix, as used in the exact
   229	conjugation equations in `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint
   230	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:314-334`, paper
   231	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1713`. -/
   232	noncomputable def conjBy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
   233	    (V N : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   234	  V * N * Vᴴ
   235	
   236	/-- The common error scale for constructing the pulled-apart measurements from
   237	a global polynomial-pair witness. Here `deltaG` is its consistency error. The
   238	remaining terms record the point-measurement transfer
   239	and the Schwartz--Zippel loss; when `0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1`, `sqrt epsilon` also
   240	dominates terms of order `epsilon`.
   241	
   242	This makes explicit the enlargement of the error called `deltaS` in
   243	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, blueprint
   244	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:171-205`, paper
   245	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1605`. -/
   246	noncomputable def deltaConstructPaulis (C epsilon deltaG : ℝ)
   247	    (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   248	  C * (deltaG + Real.sqrt epsilon +
   249	    ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
   250	
   251	/-- The explicit extraction scale
   252	`C * (deltaS^(1/4) + md/q)` from `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
   253	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   254	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   255	noncomputable def deltaExtract (C deltaS : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   256	  C * (Real.rpow deltaS (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
   257	
   258	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Extraction by the swap unitaries
     6	
     7	The concrete swap operators below yield the Pauli extraction conclusion. The
     8	local maps are constructed from the global polynomial
     9	measurements, and all operators retain the heterogeneous Alice and Bob
    10	placements. The generalized Pauli projectors use the field and basis fixed by
    11	`P.model`.

    13	## References
    14	
    15	The extraction witness formalizes `lem:qld-unitary` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1860`.
    18	The error-form comparison formalizes `lem:qld-extraction-error-form` and
    19	supports `rem:pauli-robustness-form` in the blueprint; its paper source is
    20	lines 1855-1858 and 1868-1876.

    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-- The concrete conclusion of `lem:qld-unitary`: the two swap maps extract an
    32	EPR state and conjugate each player's total Pauli measurement to the canonical
    33	Pauli projectors. The answer sum in `pauli_close` is over
    34	`PauliRegister P`; the uniform distribution on `Unit` records that there is no
    35	average over questions.
    36	
    37	Blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`; paper
    38	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685,1827-1859`. The swap maps
    39	are `swapUnitary w .alice` and `swapUnitary w .bob`, defined from the
    40	side-indexed global measurements, and use only the basis fixed by `P.model`.
    41	-/
    42	structure ExtractionWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaS : ℝ}
    43	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaS)
    44	    (delta : ℝ) where
    45	  /-- Each swap map is a right unitary. -/
    46	  swap_right_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
    47	    swapUnitary w side * (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ = 1
    48	  /-- Each swap map is a left unitary. -/
    49	  swap_left_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
    50	    (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ * swapUnitary w side = 1
    51	  /-- The auxiliary state on registers `AA'BB'`. -/
    52	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
    53	    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    54	  /-- The auxiliary state is normalized. -/
    55	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
    56	  /-- Applying both concrete swap maps to the expanded state extracts the ideal
    57	  auxiliary-state/EPR tensor product. -/
    58	  state_close :
    59	    ‖S.applyBoth (swapUnitary w .alice) (swapUnitary w .bob) S.psiHat -
    60	        S.idealExpState aux‖ ^ 2 ≤ delta
    61	  /-- On the ideal extracted state, conjugated total-Pauli effects are close to
    62	  the canonical projectors, for both players and both Pauli bases. -/
    63	  pauli_close : ∀ (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind),
    64	    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
    65	      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
    66	        conjBy (S.placeSide side (swapUnitary w side))
    67	          (S.placePlayer side ((S.pauliMeas side W).effect h)))
    68	      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
    69	        S.placeExtractedRegister side (pauliProj W h))
    70	      (S.idealExpState aux) ≤ delta
    71	
    72	/-- `lem:qld-unitary`: the concrete swap maps admit extraction data at the
    73	explicit extraction scale applied to `deltaConstructPaulis`.
    74	
    75	This is the source-facing existence statement from blueprint
    76	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375` and paper
    77	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1860`. It introduces no transfer
    78	premise or additional basis parameter.

    81	repair the two numerical defects at paper lines 1743-1783 without changing the
    82	conclusion; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_extraction-transfer.tex`.

    84	**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the EPR projection argument and the

    86	`aux` from the EPR projection of the swapped state, use the corrected
    87	small-error case split, and combine the point-measurement consistency with the
    88	exact swap conjugation identities. -/
    89	theorem exists_extractionWitness :
    90	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
    91	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
    92	        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
    93	          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
    94	            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG),
    95	            Nonempty
    96	              (ExtractionWitness S w
    97	                (deltaExtract C
    98	                  (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q)
    99	                  P.m P.d P.q)) := by

   103	of `thm:pauli`: when `deltaG` has the form
   104	`deltaQld a b epsilon m d q`, the result is bounded by another member of that

   116	theorem deltaExtract_le_deltaQld (C a b : ℝ) (hC : 1 ≤ C) (ha : 1 < a)
   117	    (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b < 1) :
   118	    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' < 1 ∧

   120	        epsilon ≤ 1 →

   122	            (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
   123	              (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q)
   124	            P.m P.d P.q ≤
   125	          deltaQld a' b' epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by

   246	
   247	## Pattern 2: Blueprint–Lean synchronization
   248	
   249	### The three tags
   250	
   251	The blueprint (under `blueprint/src/chapter/`) uses three LaTeX commands
   252	to link to Lean:
   253	
   254	| Tag | Meaning | Example |
   255	|-----|---------|---------|
   256	| `\lean{Name}` | The corresponding Lean declaration exists | `\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal}` |
   257	| `\leanok` (statement-level) | The Lean declaration compiles and its statement matches the source or blueprint statement; it does not certify proof closure | `\leanok` |
   258	| `\leanok` (proof-level) | The proof block is fully formalized — the theorem or lemma has a complete sorry-free proof | `\lean{...}` plus `\leanok` inside `\begin{proof}` |
   259	| `\uses{label}` | The statement or proof block depends on the cited result | `\uses{thm:orthonormalization, prop:completing-to-measurement}` |
   260	
   261	Do not use statement-level `\leanok` for a source-labelled theorem whose Lean
   262	declaration is conditional on bridge, residual, repair, proof-obligation input,
   263	generic hypotheses bundle, or generic assumptions bundle
   264	data not present in the source.
   265	
   266	### Why some nodes show white in the dep graph
   267	
   268	The dependency graph at
   269	`https://LionSR.github.io/MIPStarRE/blueprint/dep_graph_document.html`
   270	color-codes theorem nodes:
   271	
   272	- **Green**: proof-level `\leanok` is present (the proof block is fully formalized)
   273	- **White** (or white-border): `\lean{}` exists but proof-level `\leanok` is absent; may carry a statement-level `\leanok` during staged development
   274	- **Gray**: No `\lean{}` tag
   275	
   276	As of the session 49 audit (2026-05-07), the web dependency graph was
   277	built from an **older** `web.paux` file.  Almost all the nodes that
   278	appeared non-green there (Ch09 pasting lemmas, Ch10 induction helpers)
   279	already have `\leanok` in the current blueprint source files.  The web
   280	build needs regeneration.
   281

   284	The former deliberate withholding cases for `thm:orthonormalization`,

   303	### The `\uses{}` convention
   304

45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :

   245	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1605`. -/

    24	/--

    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=

    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=

    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint

    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)

    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else

    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)

    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/

    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=

  1844			&= \sum_{h \neq h'} \left( \E_u \mathbf{1}[g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)] \right) \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \\
  1845			&\leq \frac{md}{q}\;.
  1846		\end{align*}
  1847		In the last line we used that for for distinct $h \neq h'$, the polynomials $g_h \neq g_{h'}$ and thus by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma can only agree on at most $md/q$ fraction of points $u \in \F_q^m$. 
  1848		
  1849		Continuing from \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}, we use the first item of the Lemma which shows that $\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$ and equivalently $\| V_\alice^\dagger \otimes V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\hat{\psi}} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, so 
  1850		\begin{align*}
  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.
  1855		Together with \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}, 
  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]
  1859		This concludes the proof of the second item of the lemma.
  1860	\end{proof}
  1861	
  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]
  1872		and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. This shows that $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$ with robustness $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. We conclude the proof by making the identification of registers $\alice \alice'$ with $\alice'$ and $\bob \bob'$ with $\bob'$ to be consistent with the statement of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. We also note that, when unpacking the dependence on parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for some universal constants $a > 1, 0 < b < 1$, as desired.
  1877	\end{proof}
