   226	/-! ## Conjugation and extraction error -/
   227	
   228	/-- Conjugation of an operator by a square matrix, as used in the exact
   229	conjugation equations in `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint
   230	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:314-334`, paper
   231	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1713`. -/
   232	noncomputable def conjBy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
   233	    (V N : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   234	  V * N * Vᴴ
   235	
   236	/-- The common error scale for constructing the pulled-apart measurements from
   237	a global polynomial-pair witness. Here `deltaG` is its consistency error. The
   238	remaining terms record the point-measurement transfer
   239	and the Schwartz--Zippel loss; when `0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1`, `sqrt epsilon` also
   240	dominates terms of order `epsilon`.
   241	
   242	This makes explicit the enlargement of the error called `deltaS` in
   243	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, blueprint
   244	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:171-205`, paper
   245	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1605`. -/
   246	noncomputable def deltaConstructPaulis (C epsilon deltaG : ℝ)
   247	    (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   248	  C * (deltaG + Real.sqrt epsilon +
   249	    ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
   250	
   251	/-- The explicit extraction scale
   252	`C * (deltaS^(1/4) + md/q)` from `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
   253	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   254	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   255	noncomputable def deltaExtract (C deltaS : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   256	  C * (Real.rpow deltaS (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
   257

     6

     8	local maps are constructed from the global polynomial
     9	measurements, and all operators retain the heterogeneous Alice and Bob
    10	placements. The generalized Pauli projectors use the field and basis fixed by
    11	`P.model`.

    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-- The concrete conclusion of `lem:qld-unitary`: the two swap maps extract an
    32	EPR state and conjugate each player's total Pauli measurement to the canonical

    34	`PauliRegister P`; the uniform distribution on `Unit` records that there is no
    35	average over questions.

    38	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685,1827-1859`. The swap maps

    42	structure ExtractionWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaS : ℝ}
    43	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaS)
    44	    (delta : ℝ) where
    45	  /-- Each swap map is a right unitary. -/
    46	  swap_right_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
    47	    swapUnitary w side * (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ = 1
    48	  /-- Each swap map is a left unitary. -/
    49	  swap_left_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
    50	    (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ * swapUnitary w side = 1

    53	    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)

    62	  the canonical projectors, for both players and both Pauli bases. -/

    64	    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
    65	      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
    66	        conjBy (S.placeSide side (swapUnitary w side))
    67	          (S.placePlayer side ((S.pauliMeas side W).effect h)))
    68	      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
    69	        S.placeExtractedRegister side (pauliProj W h))

     3	/-! # Decoding maps for the low-degree code
     4	
     5	This file supplies `def:decoding-map` and the Boolean cube embedding from
     6	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
     7	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`.  The specialization to
     8	polynomial representatives is `decodeFqRep`; its restriction to the bounded
     9	class `Poly` is defined in `Algebra/Decoding`.

    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    17	
    18	/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by
    19	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    20	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    21	def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
    22	  | false => 0
    23	  | true => 1
    24	
    25	/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
    26	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    27	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    28	def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
    29	  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)
    30	
    31	/-- On the Boolean cube, an indicator polynomial evaluates to the corresponding
    32	Kronecker delta.  This is the interpolation observation at paper lines 880-891. -/
    33	private theorem eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    34	    (y z : Cube m) :
    35	    MvPolynomial.eval (cubeEmbed (K := K) z) (indicatorPoly (K := K) y) =
    36	      if y = z then 1 else 0 := by
    37	  classical
    38	  rw [indicatorPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_prod]
    39	  simp only [apply_ite, MvPolynomial.eval_X, MvPolynomial.eval_sub, map_one]
    40	  have hfactor (i : Fin m) :
    41	      (if y i then cubeEmbed (K := K) z i else 1 - cubeEmbed (K := K) z i) =
    42	        if y i = z i then 1 else 0 := by
    43	    cases hy : y i <;> cases hz : z i <;> simp_all [cubeEmbed, boolToScalar]
    44	  simp_rw [hfactor]
    45	  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
    46	  split_ifs <;> simp_all [funext_iff]
    47	
    48	/-- Evaluating a low-degree encoding at an embedded Boolean point recovers its
    49	coefficient at that point, as stated at paper line 891. -/
    50	private theorem lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    51	    (a : Cube m → K) (z : Cube m) :
    52	    lowDegreeEnc a (cubeEmbed z) = a z := by
    53	  rw [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
    54	  simp [dotProduct, indicatorVec, eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed]
    55	
    56	/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    57	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    58	noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    59	    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    60	  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    63	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    64	noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    65	    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    66	  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g
    67	
    68	/-- The full-field specialization of `decodeAt` for arbitrary polynomial
    69	representatives.  Its restriction to bounded representatives is defined in
    70	`Algebra/Decoding.lean`.
    71	Every value is retained because the filter is `H = Finset.univ`, so this is the
    72	cube-indexed evaluation of a polynomial representative.  The restricted
    73	decoder identity remains separate and is only available for encoding
    74	representatives; no unrestricted interpolation identity is asserted here.
    75	
    76	This is the `H = \F_q` reading of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, used by Chapter 16 at
    78	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20`; paper origin
    79	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420` and
    80	the correction recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
    81	noncomputable def decodeFqRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    82	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Cube m → K :=
    83	  decodeAt (Finset.univ : Finset K) (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x g)
    84	
    85	/-- A polynomial representative lies in the low-degree encoding image when it
    86	is exactly the multilinear representative reconstructed from its full-field
    87	decoder.  This predicate is used to state the support restriction required by
    88	the Chapter 16 decoding argument; it does not identify arbitrary polynomial
    89	functions with their representatives.
    90	
    91	See `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-116`. -/
    92	def IsEncodingRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    93	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Prop :=
    94	  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFqRep g) = g
    95	
    96	/-- The restricted decoding identity in `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    97	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    98	theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    99	    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
   100	    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
   101	  funext y
   102	  simp [decodeAt, lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed, ha y]
   103	
   104	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   124	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   139	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   140	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   141	
   142	/--
   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   144	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   145	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/
   150	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   151	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   152	
   153	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Finite-dimensional state transformations
     5	
     6	This file defines the tensor and reindexing operations used for strategy
     7	distance, Magic Square rigidity, and the qudit-to-qubit isomorphism. See
     8	blueprint chapters 11--13 and the declaration-level references below.
     9	-/
    10	
    11	open scoped Matrix
    12	
    13	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    14	
    15	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    16	
    17	/-- Conjugation by the local isometries in `thm:ms-rigidity` and
    18	`lem:pauli-binary`; blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244` and
    19	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:710-741`, paper
    20	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652` and
    21	`04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. -/
    22	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    23	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    24	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    25	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    26	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    27	  U * M * Uᴴ
    28	
    29	/-- Coordinate transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    30	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    31	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    32	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    33	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    34	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    35	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    36	
    37	/-- Apply the two independent local isometries of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    38	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    39	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    40	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    41	    {ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
    42	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    43	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
    44	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
    45	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
    46	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    47	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB) :=
    48	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (κA × κB) ℂ).symm
    49	    (fun p =>
    50	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    51	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κA ℂ)
    52	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    53	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κB ℂ)
    54	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    55	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)))
    56	
    57	/-- Coordinate tensor used in the ideal state of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    58	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    59	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    60	noncomputable def vecTensor {ι κ : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
    62	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) :
    63	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × κ) :=
    64	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ι × κ) ℂ).symm
    65	    (fun p => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ u) p.1 * (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ v) p.2)
    66	
    67	/-- Operator transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    68	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    69	def reindexOp {ι ι' : Type*} (e : ι ≃ ι') (M : Op ι') : Op ι :=
    70	  (Matrix.reindex e.symm e.symm) M
    71	
    72	/-- Four-factor tensor shuffle used by `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    73	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    74	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    75	def prodShuffle {α β γ δ : Type*} :
    76	    (α × β) × (γ × δ) ≃ (α × γ) × (β × δ) where
    77	  toFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    78	  invFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    79	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    80	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    81	
    82	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Expanded registers and point measurements
     6	
     7	This module adjoins two EPR pairs to a heterogeneous Pauli-basis-test strategy,
     8	records the four register placements used in the analysis, and defines the
     9	expanded point observables and measurements.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The constructions formalize `def:expanded-state`, `def:expanded-observables`,
    14	`def:expanded-point-measurement`, and `def:expanded-point-trace-projection` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-874`. Their paper source is
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-418`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- The six registers `AA'A''BB'B''`, retaining distinct Alice and Bob local
    28	spaces. This is the register index type of `def:expanded-state`, paper
    29	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    30	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    31	abbrev SixReg (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    32	  (ιA × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    33	    (ιB × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P))
    34	
    35	/-- Equality of six-register indices is supplied by classical decidability for
    36	the register type. This is the index set of `def:expanded-state`; blueprint
    37	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    38	noncomputable instance sixRegDecidableEq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    39	    (ιA ιB : Type*) : DecidableEq (SixReg P ιA ιB) :=
    40	  Classical.decEq _
    41	
    42	/-- Reassociate the tensor product of the strategy state and two EPR states
    43	directly into register order `AA'A''BB'B''` for
    44	`eq:def-psihat`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`. -/
    45	def sixRegShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    46	    (((ιA × ιB) × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    47	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    48	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    49	    (p.1.1.2, (p.2.1, p.2.2)))
    50	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    51	    (p.2.2.1, p.2.2.2))
    52	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    54	
    55	/-- The four placements `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, and `AB''` used explicitly in
    56	the chapter-14 consistency statements. Paper
    57	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
    58	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
    59	inductive Placement where
    60	  | AA'
    61	  | BA''
    62	  | BB'
    63	  | AB''
    64	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    65	
    66	/-- The strategy-player side supplying the local Hilbert space in each of the
    67	four register placements at paper
    68	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`. -/
    69	def Placement.side : Placement → PlayerSide
    70	  | .AA' => .alice
    71	  | .BA'' => .bob
    72	  | .BB' => .bob
    73	  | .AB'' => .alice
    74	
    75	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    76	
    77	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    78	
    79	/-- A strategy-local register paired with one generalized-Pauli register. This
    80	is the operator space in `def:expanded-observables`, paper
    81	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`. -/
    82	abbrev ExpandedLocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :=
    83	  S.LocalSpace side × PauliRegister P
    84	
    85	/-- The strategy state tensored with EPR states on `A'A''` and `B'B''`, in the
    86	six-register order. This is `eq:def-psihat`, paper
    87	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    88	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    89	noncomputable def psiHat (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    90	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    91	  classical
    92	  exact
    93	    reindexState (sixRegShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    94	      (vecTensor
    95	        (vecTensor S.toStrategy.ψ (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    96	        (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    97	
    98	/-- Place an operator on one of `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, or `AB''`, with the
    99	identity on all remaining registers. The input local space is determined by
   100	the placement, so no equality between the player spaces is assumed. Paper
   101	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
   102	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
   103	noncomputable def place (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   104	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   105	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   106	  fun i j =>
   107	    match p with
   108	    | .AA' =>
   109	        O (i.1.1, i.1.2.1) (j.1.1, j.1.2.1) *
   110	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   111	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   112	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   113	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   114	    | .BA'' =>
   115	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   116	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   117	          O (i.2.1, i.1.2.2) (j.2.1, j.1.2.2) *
   118	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   119	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   120	    | .BB' =>
   121	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   122	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   123	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   124	          O (i.2.1, i.2.2.1) (j.2.1, j.2.2.1) *
   125	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   126	    | .AB'' =>
   127	        O (i.1.1, i.2.2.2) (j.1.1, j.2.2.2) *
   128	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   129	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   130	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   131	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1
   132	
   133	/-- The expanded observable
   134	`W^r(u) tensor tau^W(r * ind_m(u))` on a selected player side. This is
   135	Equation `eq:lc-23`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`,
   136	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:783-807`. -/
   137	noncomputable def expObs (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (r : PauliScalar P) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   139	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   140	  heteroKron (S.pointObs side W r u)
   141	    (tauObservable W (fun h => r * indicatorVec u h))
   142	
   143	/-- The Fourier average defining the expanded point effect. This is the first
   144	display of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   145	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   146	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   147	noncomputable def expPointOp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   148	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   149	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   150	  averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) fun r =>
   151	    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)) • S.expObs side W r u
   152	
   153	/-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding has
   154	value `a` at `u`. This is Equation `eq:qld-point-obs-def`, paper
   155	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:389-394`, blueprint
   156	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   157	noncomputable def tauPointProj (W : PauliKind)
   158	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=
   159	  ∑ h ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun h : PauliRegister P =>
   160	      dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = a),
   161	    pauliProj W h
   162	
   163	/-- Expanded point effects are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity
   164	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   165	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   166	theorem expPointOp_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   167	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   168	    0 ≤ S.expPointOp side W u a := by
   169	  sorry
   170	
   171	/-- Expanded point effects sum to the identity. This is the completeness
   172	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   173	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   174	theorem expPointOp_sum_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   175	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   176	    ∑ a, S.expPointOp side W u a = 1 := by
   177	  sorry
   178	
   179	/-- The complete expanded point measurement on the chosen player and Pauli
   180	register. Its effects are those of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   181	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   182	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   183	noncomputable def pointMeasExp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   184	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   185	    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   186	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (S.expPointOp side W u)
   187	    (S.expPointOp_nonneg side W u) (S.expPointOp_sum_eq_one side W u)
   188	
   189	/-- The expanded point effect is the convolution of the strategy point
   190	measurement and the Pauli-register point projection. This is the final display
   191	of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   192	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   193	theorem expPointOp_eq_convolution (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   194	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   195	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
   196	    S.expPointOp side W u a =
   197	      ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
   198	          p.1 + p.2 = a),
   199	        heteroKron ((S.pointMeas side W u).effect p.1)
   200	          (tauPointProj W u p.2) := by
   201	  sorry
   202	
   203	/-- The expanded point measurement is projective, as asserted after the
   204	convolution formula in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   205	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   206	theorem pointMeasExp_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   207	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   208	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.pointMeasExp side W u) := by
   209	  sorry
   210	
   211	/-- Trace-coarse-graining of the expanded point measurement. This is Equation
   212	`eq:qld-def-mptur`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`,
   213	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   214	noncomputable def expPointTrace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   215	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   216	    (r : PauliScalar P) : Measurement (ZMod 2) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   217	  (S.pointMeasExp side W u).postprocess fun a => fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)
   218	
   219	/-- Fourier inversion writes a trace-coarse-grained point effect as one half
   220	of the identity plus its signed expanded observable. This is Equation
   221	`eq:lc-22`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`, blueprint
   222	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   223	theorem expPointTrace_eq_half_add (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   224	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   225	    (r : PauliScalar P) (b : ZMod 2) :
   226	    (S.expPointTrace side W u r).effect b =
   227	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   228	        (1 + phaseSign b • S.expObs side W r u) := by
   229	  sorry
   230	
   231	end ProjectiveSetting
   232	
   233	end
   234	
   235	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5	/-! # State-dependent consistency and strategy closeness
     6	
     7	The definitions are the finite-dimensional forms of `def:consistency` and
     8	`def:strategy-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-237`,
     9	from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-288`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    17	
    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    30	
    31	/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ
    39	
    40	/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
    55	
    56	/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
    57	local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
    58	evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
    59	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    75	
    76	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     5	
     6	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     7	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     8	estimates to later proof stages.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    15	-/

    24	/--
    25	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    26	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    28	-/
    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    38	-/
    39	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    43	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
    45	
    46	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5	/-!
     6	# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states
     7	
     8	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     9	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
    10	operator algebra.  The observable/projector expansions are obtained from
    11	finite-field Fourier orthogonality in characteristic two.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    16	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    27	
    28	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    29	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    30	
    31	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    32	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    34	-/
    35	inductive PauliKind where
    36	  | X
    37	  | Z
    38	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    39	
    40	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    41	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    42	
    43	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    44	character in their statement types. -/
    45	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    46	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    47	
    48	private theorem phaseSign_eq_ffChar (t : ZMod 2) :
    49	    phaseSign t = ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2) t := by
    50	  by_cases ht : t = 0
    51	  · subst t
    52	    rw [phaseSign, if_pos rfl]
    53	    exact (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2)).map_zero_eq_one.symm
    54	  · have hval : t.val = 1 := by
    55	      have hval_ne : t.val ≠ 0 := (ZMod.val_ne_zero t).mpr ht
    56	      have hval_lt : t.val < 2 := ZMod.val_lt t
    57	      omega
    58	    have ht_one : t = 1 := (ZMod.val_eq_one (by omega) t).mp hval
    59	    subst t
    60	    rw [phaseSign, if_neg one_ne_zero]
    61	    change (-1 : ℂ) = ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2) ((1 : ℤ) : ZMod 2)
    62	    rw [ZMod.stdAddChar_coe]
    63	    convert Complex.exp_pi_mul_I.symm using 1
    64	    all_goals ring_nf
    65	
    66	private theorem phaseSign_add (s t : ZMod 2) :
    67	    phaseSign (s + t) = phaseSign s * phaseSign t := by
    68	  rw [phaseSign_eq_ffChar, phaseSign_eq_ffChar, phaseSign_eq_ffChar]
    69	  exact (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2)).map_add_eq_mul s t
    70	
    71	private theorem star_phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : star (phaseSign t) = phaseSign t := by
    72	  by_cases ht : t = 0 <;> simp [phaseSign, ht]
    73	
    74	private theorem phaseSign_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → ZMod 2) :
    75	    phaseSign (∑ i, f i) = ∏ i, phaseSign (f i) := by
    76	  classical
    77	  induction (Finset.univ : Finset ι) using Finset.induction_on with
    78	  | empty => simp [phaseSign]
    79	  | @insert i s hi ih =>
    80	      rw [Finset.sum_insert hi, Finset.prod_insert hi, phaseSign_add, ih]

     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.

    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.

    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52

    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint

    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=

    62	
    63	/--

   814	\section{Expanding the Hilbert space and defining commuting observables}
   815	\label{sec:expanding}
   816	
   817	The next step of the analysis adjoins ancillary EPR registers to the
   818	players' state and lifts the strategy observables and measurements to the
   819	expanded state. The point of the construction is that the ancilla factor of
   820	each lifted observable carries the \emph{exact} Pauli commutation sign, so
   821	that the signs cancel and the lifted observables approximately commute for
   822	every tuple $\omega$.
   823	
   824	\begin{definition}[Expanded state]
   825		\label{def:expanded-state}
   826		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SixReg, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.psiHat}
   827		\leanok
   828		\uses{lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:EPR}
   829		Recall that $M = 2^m$. Introduce registers $\mathsf{A}', \mathsf{A}'',
   830		\mathsf{B}', \mathsf{B}''$, each with Hilbert space isomorphic to
   831		$(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, and define the state
   832		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-psihat}
   833			\ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}
   834			\,=\, (\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}
   835			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''}
   836			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}\,,
   837		\end{equation}
   838		where $\ket{\psi}$ is the extended strategy state of the strategy
   839		under analysis (Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the
   840		convention following it) and
   841		$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ is the maximally entangled state on
   842		$\C^q \ot \C^q$ (Definition~\ref{def:EPR}). For the remainder of this
   843		chapter, as well as in Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining}
   844		and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}, all approximations $\approx$ and
   845		$\simeq$ are evaluated with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$,
   846		unless stated otherwise.
   847	\end{definition}
   848	
   849	\begin{definition}[Expanded observables]
   850		\label{def:expanded-observables}
   851		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.expObs}

   434	\paragraph{Partitioning the registers, and symmetries}
   435	In the remainder of this section as well as \Cref{sec:combining,sec:apply-ldt}, we will partition the six registers
   436	$\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''$ into
   437	two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first is to consider
   438	$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
   443	registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two
   444	operators $M, N$ will hold for both of the two bipartitioning schemes,
   445	and with the first and second party interchanged. That is, whenever we
   446	derive a bipartite relation of the form
   447	\[ M_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\delta N_{\bob \alice''}, \]
   448	the same steps, with the registers appropriately changed, will also
   449	yield
   450	\begin{align*}
   451	  N_{\alice \alice'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\bob \alice''}, \\
   452	  M_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} N_{\alice \bob''}, \\
   453	  N_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\alice \bob''}.
   454	\end{align*}
   455	
   456	Similarly, whenever we derive a single-party relation of the form
   457	$M_{\alice \alice'} \approx N_{\alice \alice'}$, the same steps with
   458	the registers appropriately changed will also yield the same relation
   459	on $\bob\alice''$, $\bob \bob'$ and $\alice \bob''$. We refer to these
   460	relations as \emph{symmetric equivalents}.

   207	## 8. Concurrency
   208	
   209	| Lock | Key | Cancellation |
   210	|---|---|---|
   211	| review | PR id | none — a queued run waits, then re-checks the head |
   212	| fix (`autofix.md`) | branch | supersession sentinel |
   213	
   214	The split of keys is inherited (`pr-review.yml:18-20` groups by PR number with
   215	`cancel-in-progress: false`; `auto-fix.yml:259-261` groups by head branch with
   216	`cancel-in-progress: true`) and it matters: cancelling a review wastes the
   217	tokens already spent and produces nothing, whereas cancelling a superseded fix
   218	saves a write to a branch that has already moved.
   219	
   220	Locks are directories under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` holding the
   221	holder's pid — `flock(1)` does not exist on macOS.  A lock whose holder is gone
   222	is reclaimed.  After acquiring the review lock, `review.sh` re-reads the local
   223	tip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued
   224	invalidates the review, and the run exits without a verdict rather than
   225	describing a commit that is no longer head.  The same check runs again after
   226	the agent returns; a head that moved during the review makes the result stale
   227	and forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.
   228	
   229	`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.
   230	The two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh
   231	checkout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being
   232	rewritten under it.

   234	## 9. The findings ledger
   235	
   236	`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
   237	review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
   238	`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
   239	`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
   240	GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
   241	status signal; the REST `line` field lied.
   242	
   243	Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
   244	`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
   245	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:
   246	
   247	    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis
   248	
   249	| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
   250	|---|---|---|
   251	| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
   252	| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
   253	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   254	
   255	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   256	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   257	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   258	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   259	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   260	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.
   261	
   262	**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
   263	not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
   264	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   265	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   266	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   267	must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
   268	and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
   269	is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
   270	decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
   271	without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
   272	repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
   273	A PR that touches only the workflow layer (`local/`, `.githooks/`,
   274	`scripts/tests/`, `docs/`, telemetry) is adjudicated after its SECOND round
   275	because reviewer rounds on scaffolding did not converge (events.md
   276	2026-09-03); a further review is still permitted when the head changed (an
   277	adjudication needs an exact-head review), but it is churn the owner's
   278	watchdog reports.  Mathematics PRs keep the four-round cap above.
   279	
   280	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   281	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   282	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
   283	all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
   284	next review re-derives from the new diff.
   285	
   286	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   287	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   288	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not

   290	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   291	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

   390	## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)
   391	
   392	A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
   393	the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:
   394	
   395	1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   396	   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   397	   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   398	   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   399	   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   400	   `moot: <reason>`);
   401	2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
   402	3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
   403	4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   404	   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.
   405	
   406	Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
   407	This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
   408	terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.
   409	
   410	## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)
   411	
   412	The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
   413	every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
   414	change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
   415	sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
   416	so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
   417	earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
   418	published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict
   419	and ledger as the exact-head review of the new head, marked "Carried forward
   420	from <sha>" (marker `<!-- mipstarre-review-carried from=<sha> -->`; a carried
   421	review is not a review round and is never itself a carry source), and posts the matching
   422	`local-review/summary` — without dispatching the reviewer.  Adverse verdicts
   423	are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
   424	change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
   425	patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.

   247	## Pattern 2: Blueprint–Lean synchronization
   248	
   249	### The three tags
   250	
   251	The blueprint (under `blueprint/src/chapter/`) uses three LaTeX commands
   252	to link to Lean:
   253	
   254	| Tag | Meaning | Example |
   255	|-----|---------|---------|
   256	| `\lean{Name}` | The corresponding Lean declaration exists | `\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal}` |
   257	| `\leanok` (statement-level) | The Lean declaration compiles and its statement matches the source or blueprint statement; it does not certify proof closure | `\leanok` |
   258	| `\leanok` (proof-level) | The proof block is fully formalized — the theorem or lemma has a complete sorry-free proof | `\lean{...}` plus `\leanok` inside `\begin{proof}` |
   259	| `\uses{label}` | The statement or proof block depends on the cited result | `\uses{thm:orthonormalization, prop:completing-to-measurement}` |
   260	
   261	Do not use statement-level `\leanok` for a source-labelled theorem whose Lean
   262	declaration is conditional on bridge, residual, repair, proof-obligation input,
   263	generic hypotheses bundle, or generic assumptions bundle
   264	data not present in the source.
   265	
   266	### Why some nodes show white in the dep graph
   267	
   268	The dependency graph at
   269	`https://LionSR.github.io/MIPStarRE/blueprint/dep_graph_document.html`
   270	color-codes theorem nodes:
   271	
   272	- **Green**: proof-level `\leanok` is present (the proof block is fully formalized)
   273	- **White** (or white-border): `\lean{}` exists but proof-level `\leanok` is absent; may carry a statement-level `\leanok` during staged development
   274	- **Gray**: No `\lean{}` tag
